spec.effect: plasma -- a translucent tube of ionised gas filling kitty's collapsing quad, with three thin braided filaments crawling along it into the cursor, and charged ions peeling off the path in closed-form cyclotron spirals. Designed against the UNCOMMITTED effect framework in the working tree (baud-render/src/effect.rs: Effect/Ignition/Vfx, EffectU = 24-float shared prefix + k[8], Kind::Band / Kind::Particle, Effect::ALL), not HEAD's fire-only fire.rs. Sketch: (not kept) trail/new/plasma/plasma_sketch.metal (sha256 13c2f982b7393b3f93a2380728caf64ac29786419ec7b56727a7ce4bb5dd4956). Checks: check.py (gyration closed form vs numeric integration, reach, sRGB thresholds) and area.py (WCAG concurrent-area sweep over cell height and backing scale).

prior_art.name: orbkit SHDR-13 plasma globe (filament = zero set of trig fields; brightness 1/(d2*sharp+soft); writhe rooted at the nucleus by a smoothstep; tip flare where a streamer lands)
prior_art.licence: MIT (an original orb per CREDITS.md at the same commit; the XorDev-derived orbs in that repo are non-commercial and were NOT used)
prior_art.what_to_take: The core idea: a filament is where a field crosses zero, lit by proximity to that zero, with the root pinned by a smoothstep so filaments stay attached to the electrode (here: the cursor). Time enters only as additive phase. Baud takes it in 2D: filament i is the curve w = A_i(s, age); its core is a Gaussian of (w - A_i)/W (Gaussian, not their Lorentzian, so the flash area is bounded).

prior_art.what_to_take: Sum-of-sines with each wave on its own rate, time only as additive phase so the result is a closed form of age; luminance only, no palette. Confirms the shape; baud's version keeps intensity as opacity and never cycles a palette.

prior_art.name: Second Reality (Future Crew 1993) PLZ part -- the canonical demoscene plasma, released by the authors
prior_art.licence: Unlicense (public domain), UNLICENSE at the same commit, sha256 7e12e5df4bae12cb21581ba157ced20e1986a0508dd10d0e8a4ab9a4cf94e85c
prior_art.what_to_take: The wave table psini(a) = 55 sin(a) + 5 sin(6a) + 4 sin(21a) + 64 (line 144): a dominant fundamental plus small detuned high harmonics, and PLZSINI (line 15): each term is a sine of one coordinate warped by a sine of the other, with per-frame phase offsets. Baud's filament curve is exactly that shape: 0.78-0.80 fundamental + 0.20-0.25 detuned harmonic, harmonic flowing against the fundamental. The palette rotation that makes SR colourful is the part the rule that every effect is the cursor's colour forbids, and is not taken.

prior_art.name: Neovide cursor VFX, Railgun and Torpedo trails
prior_art.what_to_take: Railgun (lines 328-372): particles placed along the travel at t, initial velocity direction a phase of t, velocity rotated at a constant curl each step (rotate_vec(speed, dt*rotation_speed), line 304) -- i.e. circular (cyclotron) motion; lifetime scaled by t so the tail dies first; count = travel/cell_height * density. Baud's ions are the same motion integrated in closed form with drag, which Neovide steps per frame.

spec.look:
Frame by frame, for a 30-column hop on a dark theme with a white block cursor:
- Ignition (first frame after the 10 ms dwell): the quad springs out from the old cell. Inside it a faint translucent tube (the cursor's colour at ~0.28 opacity at the edge, ~0.08 more inside) and, running its length, three hair-thin bright filaments (1.5-3.5 device px wide at a 34 px cell), braided around the path's centre line, each a smooth wave a few cells long with a small kinked harmonic riding on it. Around the tube a soft sheath glow fading over about one cell.
- 0-100 ms: the filaments crawl -- their shapes flow along the tube toward the cursor at ~4-5 cells a second while their small harmonics drift the other way, so they twist past one another like the streamers in a plasma ball. Brighter knots (about +40%) stream along each filament into the cursor. All three converge onto the centre line over the last two cells and disappear into the cursor, which is left bare (the hole). Meanwhile ions are released along the path where the emitter passes: small soft dots (1.5-3.5 px radius) that shoot sideways off the tube -- half to one side, half to the other (the two charges) -- and immediately curl into tight hooks and spirals, one way or the other depending on their charge, slowing as they curl.
- 100-450 ms: the quad collapses into the cursor (kitty's leading corners first), shortening the tube and the filaments with it. The whole plasma 'starves' rather than burns: everything dims together as (1-k)^2, the filaments thin to half their width, and the sheath contracts toward the tube (its decay rate grows 2.5x). Ions complete roughly half to one full loop and fade.
- 450-650 ms: the tube has sunk into the cursor; a thin contracting glow around the cursor fades to nothing by 0.55 s; the last ions die by 0.65 s at the latest.
Distinct from fire: nothing rises; no noise; the tube is contained along the path; motion is a braided flow INTO the cursor plus sideways-curling particles; it ends by dimming and thinning, not by a burn front travelling from the tail. On a light theme with a dark cursor the same rule draws a smoky-dark tube with dark filaments and dark curling dots.
spec.design:
All in frame pixels p = in.pos.xy - origin; unit c = cell height px; k = age/LIFE.
Shared prefix (EffectU as in the working tree): c[4] quad corners this frame, hole, origin, tail, dir, len, unit, age, life = LIFE, seed, reach = REACH.

Constants: LIFE = 0.55 s. REACH = 1.0 cell. SWEEP = 0.10 s (ion births). Params k[0..7] per uniform_params.

Per pixel:
1. if in hole -> 0. if k >= 1 -> 0. d0 = fx_distance(p)/c (existing quad SDF, winding). if d0 > REACH -> 0.
2. Envelope: env = (1-k)^2 (unimodal, reaches 0 at LIFE, so the driver's end-of-effect never pops).
3. Tube: inside = 1 - smoothstep(-0.03, 0.03, d0); tube = k3*inside + k4*exp(-k5*(1+1.5k)*max(d0,0)). With k3=0.08, k4=0.20, k5=5: at d0=REACH the sheath is 0.20*e^-5 = 0.00135 < 0.5/255 -- that is where REACH = 1.0 comes from (threshold d = ln(0.20*510)/5 = 0.925).
4. Filaments only when d0 < 0.15 (the mask's support; skips the sheath-only pixels):
   H = hole centre; r = p - H; axis a = (k1,k2) (live, see below); s = -dot(r,a)/c (cells behind the head); w = (a.x r.y - a.y r.x)/c (cells across, perp = (-a.y, a.x)).
   pinch = smoothstep(0, 2.0, s); amp = k0 * 0.62 * pinch.
   wave(x) = sinpi(2*fract(x + 0.5) - 1) = sin(2*pi*x), argument folded into [-1,1).
   For i = 0..2 with table (K, F, K2, F2, M, W, G):
     i0: 0.23, 1.10, 0.71, -0.85, 0.22, 0.040, 1.00
     i1: 0.31, 1.35, 0.93, -1.05, 0.20, 0.034, 0.85
     i2: 0.17, 0.80, 0.53, +1.20, 0.25, 0.050, 0.65
     (K cycles/cell along, F cycles/s: positive F moves crests toward the head at F/K cells/s = 3.5-4.8 c/s.)
     ph_i = fx_unit(fx_hash(seed + i)); ph2_i = fx_unit(fx_hash(seed + 16 + i)); kn = fx_unit(fx_hash(seed + 8)).
     A_i = amp * ((1-M) wave(K s + ph + F age) + M wave(K2 s + ph2 + F2 age)).
     width_i = max(W (1 - 0.5k), 1.1/c).
     e = (w - A_i)/width_i.
     knot_i = 0.72 + 0.28 wave(0.45 s + kn + i/3 + k7 age).
     fil += G exp(-e^2) knot_i.
   fil = saturate(fil) * k6 * (1 - smoothstep(-0.02, 0.15, d0)).
5. alpha = color.a * saturate(env * (tube + (1 - tube) fil)); return (color.rgb*alpha, alpha) -- premultiplied OVER in the cursor's colour, no hue.

Per-frame params computed in Rust (plasma::params(&Vfx)):
- Live axis (k1,k2): C = mean of the 4 corners, H = hole centre; if |H-C| >= 0.25*unit then a = (H-C)/|H-C| else a = ignition.dir. This fixes the retarget case: within REIGNITE the driver keeps the ignition (tail/dir/len of the FIRST move) while the quad is retargeted; a path-anchored braid would lie along the old path and pinch into a cell the cursor has left. Anchoring the braid at the live hole along the live emitter follows the quad.
- half k0 = max(0.5*(|a.y|*cellW + |a.x|*cellH)/unit, 0.25): the cell's half-extent across the axis. From the CELL size, not the hole (a bar cursor's hole is ~2 px wide and would collapse a vertical move's braid onto the axis). Needs the cell width on Ignition (see risks).
- Filament gain k6 = min(0.95, 0.094*exp(q^2)), q = 0.8*21824 / (6 * W_css * L_css), W_css = max(0.05*unit, 1.1)/scale, L_css = len/scale. Needs the backing scale on Vfx. Leaves the gain at 0.95 for moves under ~100 cells at a 17-CSS-px cell (2x), then dims the filaments so their concurrent flash area never exceeds 80% of WCAG's 21,824 CSS px^2, at every font size and scale (area.py: worst case 0.80 of the limit on light themes, 0.52-0.53 on dark, for cell heights 14-40 CSS px at 1x and 2x). A cap in cells instead (0.95*min(1,(80/L)^2)) was checked and fails from 24 CSS-px cells up (1.22-3.39 of the limit), so it is rejected.

End rule: end() = max(LIFE, max over ions of born + life) in [0.55, 0.65] s (born <= 0.10, life <= 0.55). The driver is unchanged: ignition on a long move (>2 cells after the 10 ms dwell), at most three a second (REIGNITE 334 ms, a retarget within it keeps age and seed), out at end() -- and at LIFE the body is already at zero opacity, so the quad vanishing with it at end() is invisible even when a long diagonal chase outlasts LIFE.
spec.particles:
Ions, closed form in Rust (never in the shader; drawn as Kind::Particle discs through the existing glyph_vertex uv branch and fire_ember's disc, factored into a shared fx_particle).
Count n = clamp(round(len/unit * 3), 8, 64) -- fewer than fire's 8/unit; the tube carries the look.
Ion j: h0 = Hash(seed ^ j*0x9E3779B9).next(), h1..h6 = successive .next() (the same derivation as fire's embers).
- along = h0.unit(); born = along * SWEEP (0.10 s); life = 0.25 + 0.30*h1.unit().
- charge q = +1 if h2.unit() < 0.5 else -1.
- p0 = tail + dir*len*along + perp*(h3.unit() - 0.5)*0.6*unit, perp = (-dir.y, dir.x).
- speed = (1.8 + 2.4*h4.unit()) * unit per second; direction = (q*perp) rotated by (h5.unit() - 0.5)*pi/2; plus carry = dir * min(len/SWEEP, 40*unit) * 0.03. v0 = speed*direction + carry.
- Motion: velocity decays and rotates, v(a) = v0 e^{-D a} R(omega a), D = 2.5 /s, omega = q * 2*pi*2.0 rad/s (two turns a second; charge sets the sense; on the y-down screen positive omega turns x toward +y, i.e. clockwise).
- Position at age a = ignition.age - born (0 <= a <= life): E = exp(-D a), C = cos(omega a), S = sin(omega a), den = D^2 + omega^2,
  Mr = (D(1 - E C) + omega E S)/den, Mi = (omega(1 - E C) - D E S)/den,
  centre = p0 + (Mr v0.x - Mi v0.y, Mi v0.x + Mr v0.y). (The complex form of p0 + v0 (e^{(-D+i omega)a} - 1)/(-D + i omega); check.py matches a 200,000-step numeric integration to 1e-11 at a = 0.1, 0.3, 0.55; small-a limit is p0 + v0 a.) Gyration radius |v0|/sqrt(D^2+omega^2) = 0.14-0.33 cells; 0.5-1.1 turns over a life.
- heat = 1 - a/life; glow = 0.85 * heat^1.5 (monotone, no twinkle); radius = unit*(0.040 + 0.035*h6.unit())*(0.55 + 0.45*heat).
- Retarget caveat: ions are born along the IGNITION's path through its first 0.1 s; a retarget inside that window births the late ones along a path the emitter no longer takes (fire's embers share this).

uniform_params.name: k[0] half
uniform_params.value: max(0.5*(|a.y|*cellW + |a.x|*cellH)/unit, 0.25); PER FRAME (depends on the live axis)
uniform_params.meaning: The cell's half-extent across the live axis, in cells; the braid swings to 0.62 of it. From the cell size, not the hole, so a bar cursor's vertical move does not collapse the braid.

uniform_params.name: k[1] ax
uniform_params.value: (H - C).x / |H - C| if |H - C| >= 0.25*unit, else ignition.dir.x; PER FRAME
uniform_params.meaning: Live axis x: H = hole centre, C = mean of the four quad corners this frame. Follows a retarget, which the ignition's tail/dir/len do not.

uniform_params.name: k[2] ay
uniform_params.value: same rule, y component; PER FRAME

uniform_params.name: k[3] tube
uniform_params.meaning: Extra opacity inside the quad (the body fill). May be set to 0 for 'sheath and filaments only'.

uniform_params.name: k[4] sheath
uniform_params.meaning: Sheath opacity at the quad's edge (and inside, added to k[3]): max body opacity 0.28.

uniform_params.name: k[5] decay
uniform_params.meaning: Sheath e-fold rate at ignition; multiplied by (1 + 1.5k) as the plasma cools, so the sheath contracts. Fixes REACH = 1.0 (0.20*e^-5 < 0.5/255).

uniform_params.name: k[6] fil
uniform_params.value: min(0.95, 0.094*exp(q^2)), q = 0.8*21824/(6*W_css*L_css), W_css = max(0.05*unit, 1.1)/scale, L_css = len/scale; PER FRAME (needs the backing scale on Vfx)
uniform_params.meaning: Filament gain with the WCAG concurrent-area cap built in: 0.95 for ordinary moves, dimming only on very long ones so the thin-line flash area stays <= 80% of 21,824 CSS px^2 at any font size (area.py).

uniform_params.name: k[7] knot
uniform_params.meaning: Knot flow: how often a brightness knot passes a fixed pixel on a filament (knots stream into the cursor at 2.5/0.45 = 5.6 cells/s).

spec.life_seconds: LIFE (body) 0.55 s; end() = max(LIFE, last ion's born + life) in [0.55, 0.65] s. Envelope (1-k)^2 is 0 at LIFE, so the driver dropping the quad at end() is invisible even when a long diagonal chase outlasts it.
spec.photosensitivity:
Blend space checked: the targets are BGRA8Unorm (metal.rs 520 etc.), not an _srgb format, with the surface tagged sRGB, so premultiplied OVER blends sRGB-encoded values; encoded alpha a of white over black is linear ((a+0.055)/1.055)^2.4.
1. Large-area change: the tube/sheath and the ignition itself follow ONE unimodal envelope (1-k)^2 per ignition -- one general flash at most -- and the driver lights at most three ignitions a second (REIGNITE 334 ms; a retarget within it keeps the same ignition and age, so no new flash). This is fire's shipped argument, and it is the claim made here. It is NOT claimed that the tube is sub-threshold in general: over near-black ground 0.28 encoded is 0.064 linear (< 0.10), but over glass or a mid-grey ground, or dark-on-light, the same opacity moves relative luminance by more than 0.10 (e.g. ~0.15 around encoded 0.5; dark 0.28 over white takes 1.0 to 0.48).
2. No global pulse anywhere: no term modulates the whole tube in time (unlike fielding's 6.4 Hz thickness pulse, which is the pattern to avoid). All intra-ignition temporal modulation -- the filaments' crawl, the knots, the ions -- lives in thin structures.
3. Thin structures under WCAG's concurrent-area rule: a filament core only exceeds the 10% threshold within +/-1.02 W (dark theme, encoded >= 0.35) or +/-1.54 W (light theme, darker state < 0.80 needs encoded dark >= 0.094) of its centre line; Gaussian cores (not Lorentzian) make that width finite. Three filaments x that width x the tube length is the worst-case concurrent flashing area; k[6] caps the gain in CSS pixels so this stays <= 0.8 x 21,824 CSS px^2 for every cell height and backing scale (area.py: max 0.80 light, 0.53 dark). The tube also shortens within ~0.1-0.4 s as the quad collapses, so long lengths are brief. Ions are discs of radius <= 0.075 cell with monotone fades (no twinkle).
4. Per-pixel reading (stricter): at a fixed pixel inside the braid, filament i's fundamental crosses it up to 2F_i times a second (2.2, 2.7, 1.6), the counter-flowing harmonics add wiggles, and knots pass at 2.5 Hz: worst case roughly 6-9 crossings plus 2.5 knots a second, i.e. up to ~6 thin-line events at one pixel within a 0.55 s ignition. Under a reading where every pixel event counts, this design does NOT comply; a compliant variant is F = (0.45, 0.55, 0.35), F2 = 0, knots off (sum of 2F = 2.7/s), which looks near-static over a 0.55 s life. Raised as an open question.
spec.rust_reference_notes:
Port for the pixel oracle (baud-present-macos/tests/cells.rs, next to fire_reference), composited over the renderer's own records as fire's is:
- fx_distance: already ported for fire (the winding quad SDF); reuse it.
- fx_hash / fx_unit: already ported as `Word::hash` / `Word::unit`; phases are Word(seed + i).hash().unit(), seed + 16 + i, seed + 8 (wrapping adds).
- wave(x): MSL fract is x - floor(x) clamped to 0x1.fffffep-1; Rust f32::fract truncates toward zero and is WRONG for negative x. Port as `let f = (x - x.floor()).min(1.0 - f32::EPSILON / 2.0); (core::f32::consts::PI * (2.0 * f - 1.0)).sin()`. The argument is thereby always in [-pi, pi).
- sinpi precision: fast-math sinpi is good to 2^-13 absolute on [-1,1] (MSL spec table). The steepest term is the Gaussian core: an error of 2^-13 x 0.31 cells in A_i, divided by the narrowest width (0.034 cells, or the 1.1 px floor = 0.032 cells at a 34 px cell), is ~1.2e-3 in e, and |d exp(-e^2)/de| <= 0.86 gives ~1e-3 in alpha against 3.9e-3 for one step of 255 -- about a 4x margin. At a 68 px cell (zoom) the floor drops to 0.016 cells and the margin to ~1.7x. If the one-step tolerance fails there, use `precise::sinpi` in px_wave (9 calls a filament pixel) -- that is the fallback, and it is local.
- exp: fast exp is <= 3 + floor(2|x|) ulp relative; the Gaussian's exp(-e^2) is only relevant where e^2 < ~6 (below that it is < 1/255 of anything), so the relative error there is <= 15 ulp ~ 1e-6. Sheath exp argument <= 12.5. No huge arguments anywhere; the phase arguments are folded by fract before sinpi (s is at most ~120-150 cells; K2*s ~ 140 cycles keeps ~16 fractional bits after fract).
- smoothstep, saturate, mix: as fire's port. d0 early outs (> REACH, filaments only when d0 < 0.15) must be ported identically, including the strict/non-strict comparisons.
- Params k[0..7] come from the renderer's uniform (read, not recomputed), but the Rust functions that compute the live axis, half and the k[6] cap get their own unit tests (axis follows a retarget; fallback to ignition.dir when |H-C| < 0.25 cell; cap keeps 3*width*L <= 0.8*21,824 CSS px^2 across cell heights 14-40 and scales 1-2, mirroring area.py).
- Ions: the reference composites the renderer's Kind::Particle records (as fire's embers), so no port of the gyration is needed there; a unit test in plasma.rs holds the closed form to a fine numeric integration (as check.py does) and to its a -> 0 limit p0 + v0 a.
- Oracle scenes: as fire's -- a fire across and one down at four ages in a letterboxed target -- plus a retarget scene (axis != ignition.dir) and a light-theme scene; every pixel outside the records equals the frame without the effect; no colour past alpha.
spec.cost_vs_fire: Estimated, not measured. Per pixel in a band: fire does two fx_distance calls, a 4-octave value-noise fbm (32 PCG hashes, 4 quintic fades, 16 lerps) and several smoothsteps. Plasma does ONE fx_distance, then for sheath-only pixels (d0 >= 0.15, most of the band) just a smoothstep and an exp; only pixels inside or within 0.15 cell of the quad pay the braid: 7 PCG hashes (seed phases; could be hoisted if the framework allowed per-draw constants), 9 sinpi, 3 exp, 3 divides. Record area is also smaller: REACH 1.0 cell vs fire's 2.0 (fire::REACH = HEIGHT + 0.4), so a horizontal hop's bands cover ~3 cell-rows of height instead of ~5. Ions: 3 a cell (8..64) vs fire's 8 a cell (16..160) embers, same disc. Guess: 25-35% of fire's fragment cost. To be measured the way fire's ember branch was: frame_gpu's instance arm, base vs plasma built at one scratch path, an A/A copy, launches rotated, GPU-busy column.
risks: Targets the UNCOMMITTED effect framework in the working tree (effect.rs with Effect/Ignition/Vfx, EffectU = 24-float prefix + k[8], Kind::Band/Kind::Particle, Effect::ALL/COUNT/index/fragment/reach/life/params/end/particles), not HEAD's fire.rs; if that framework changes before this lands, re-fit the uniform.

Framework change 1: Effect::params is `const fn params(self) -> [f32; PARAMS]`; plasma needs `params(self, vfx: &Vfx)` for the live axis, half and the length cap (fire ignores the argument). Vfx::uniform calls it.

Framework change 2: Ignition carries only `unit` (cell height). `half` needs the cell width: Ignition::ignite must take the driver's `cell: (f32, f32)` (the driver already has it at ignite) and fire's tests change with the signature.

Framework change 3: the k[6] area cap needs the backing scale on Vfx (or passed to params); without it, fall back to stating the cell-height range the bound holds for (a cap in cells fails from 24 CSS-px cells up, 1.22-3.39x the WCAG area on light themes, area.py).
Framework change 4: fx_particle does not exist; factor fire_ember's body into it and call it from both fire_fragment and plasma_fragment (the sketch calls fire_ember until then).

Adding `plasma` to the config reader will fail `the_cursor_page_shows_every_trail` (docs/cursor.md + docs/cursor.html must show every trail the reader knows) until a clip and a still are recorded with scripts/trail-clips.sh and added to both pages; also CursorTrail/Style mapping, config tests, the metallib test that every Effect::ALL fragment is in the library (metallib.rs ~239), and the .metallib must be rebuilt with scripts/build-metallib.sh.

Axis fallback: when the hole centre is within 0.25 cell of the corners' mean the axis is the ignition's dir; the fallback is invisible only if the quad mask and the hole cover everything the braid would draw then. Propose a unit test holding the filament term at zero outside the hole in that state.

The live axis direction jumps at a retarget (the hole jumps to the new cursor while the corners are continuous), so the braid's layout can pop at that frame -- the quad's own shape changes direction there too; judge it on the clip.
Ions born within 0.1 s along the ignition's path: a retarget inside that window births the late ones along a path the emitter no longer takes (fire's embers share this).
The sinpi tolerance margin shrinks with the pixel floor at large cells (~1.7x at a 68 px cell); precise::sinpi is the fallback if the oracle's one-step tolerance fails at zoom.
The 25-35%-of-fire cost is an estimate until measured with frame_gpu's GPU-busy column.
Photosensitivity compliance is claimed only under WCAG's concurrent-area reading plus fire's per-ignition count; under a per-pixel reading it does not comply (see open questions).
open_questions: Photosensitivity policy: does thin-line motion inside one ignition count per pixel, or by WCAG's concurrent area? By area it complies (k[6] caps the filaments' concurrent flash area at <= 80% of 21,824 CSS px^2 on light themes, 53% on dark, at every cell height 14-40 CSS px and scale 1-2). Per pixel it does not: a pixel in the braid sees up to ~6-9 filament crossings plus 2.5 knot passes a second (at most ~6 events in a 0.55 s ignition). The per-pixel-compliant variant (F = 0.45/0.55/0.35 Hz, no harmonic flow, no knots) looks nearly static over the life. Which reading governs?

Body: a faint solid fill across the quad (k[3] = 0.08, ~0.28 total with the sheath) reads close to the quad trail, dimmer. Alternative: sheath and filaments only (k[3] = 0), which reads more like a plasma ball's streamers and less like a smear. Which?

Font-size-dependent dimming: to hold the area bound, k[6] dims the filaments on very long moves (below ~100 cells at a 17-CSS-px cell nothing dims; at 150 cells gain ~0.57, at 200 ~0.26). Accept the dimming, or cap the filaments' length instead (e.g. draw them only within N cells of the cursor)?
Flow direction: filaments and knots flow INTO the cursor (the cursor as the electrode the discharge lands on). Or away from it, toward where the cursor came from?
Ions: both charges (half curl clockwise, half anticlockwise) or one sense for all? And keep them at all, or let the braid carry the effect alone?
departures: The hand (built after this spec, recorded here and in note W section 5.5). This spec takes the braid's offset across the axis, w = (a.x r.y - a.y r.x)/c, and the ions' launch side perp = (-dir.y, dir.x), their launch turn and their spin omega = q 2 pi 2.0 relative to the move's axis, so a leftward move is the rightward one turned a half turn rather than mirrored: its filaments cross the other way and its ions curl to the other side, and a cursor moved left and back draws two different trails. The build gives each ignition a hand, left for an ignition moving left (dir.x < 0) and right otherwise, and a left hand negates w, perp, the turn and omega, and snaps an ion's disc box from the mirror image of floor, ceil(cx + side/2) - side. A rightward or vertical move keeps every bit this spec gives it; the same seed moving left draws the rightward frame mirrored, every pixel. Reason: a trail has to look the same whichever way the cursor moves along a line. Up and down moves keep this spec's sense, turned over rather than mirrored.

The ignition rule (recorded here and in note W section 5.5). This spec keeps the driver's rule: at most three ignitions a second (REIGNITE 334 ms), a long move within it retargeting the quad and keeping the ignition's age and seed. The build lights the plasma on every long move instead, so a move soon after the last draws a fresh plasma rather than the burning one at its age, whose envelope (1-k)^2 is 0.67 of a fresh one's 0.1 s after it lit, 0.41 at 0.2 s and 0.21 at 0.3 s. Reason: a quick move is drawn as bright as a slow one. The flash bound holds without the guard: under the size gate WCAG 2.3.1's area clause passes every case the census counts, and over it the ledger draws every repeat under the thresholds, now clamped at the cap rather than scaled by it (note AL section 4.2). Every other effect keeps the rule.

problems: NUB AHEAD OF THE CURSOR (a real visual defect). Ahead of the head, s < 0, so the pinch smoothstep(0,2,s) is 0, amp is 0, and all three filaments lie on w = 0. The only fade left is the 0.15-cell d0 taper, so a bright spike pokes out of the cursor's leading edge. Measured on this Mac's GPU, horizontal hop at a 34 px cell, alpha /255 on the centre row at 0-4 px past the hole's right edge: 208, 166, 115, 65, 30 at age 0.02; 137, 109, 74, 41 at 0.12; 66, 53, 36, 19 at 0.25. After the corners land (quad == hole) there is a nub on each side: 46, 37, 24 at 0.3 s. With a white block cursor this reads as a spike on the cursor. Harness: (not kept) review-plasma/dump.swift. Images: review-plasma/chase-0.06-612x238.png and landed-0.3-612x238.png (dark theme on top, baud light 0x27-on-0xEF below).

BAR AND UNDERLINE CURSORS BREAK THE BRAID, so the spec's stated rationale for k[0] is wrong. `Renderer::cursor_rect` (baud-render/src/renderer.rs:839-845) makes the smear's rect `line` px thick (max(thickness, 2)) for bar and underline, and the quad chases that rect. k[0] is taken from the cell, so a horizontal move with an underline cursor swings the braid about ±10.5 px (0.62 × 0.5 cell at 34 px) around a quad about 2 px tall. The filament gate d0 < 0.15 (about 5 px), with its taper, deletes almost all of it: what is left is short dashes where the filaments cross the axis. A vertical move with a bar cursor has the same failure. "From the CELL size, not the hole, so a bar cursor's vertical move does not collapse the braid" trades a collapse for an erasure.

WCAG MODEL USES THE WRONG DOMAIN. Pinned understanding-2.3.1.txt, lines 181-194 and the note: the thresholds pass if ANY of (a) at most 3 general flashes a second, or (b) combined concurrent flash area of at most 25% 'within any 10 degree visual field', a 341x256 px rectangle 'anywhere on the displayed screen'. So the area clause is normative on its own, and open question 1 ('per pixel or by area?') is mis-framed: WCAG defines no per-pixel reading. area.py multiplies by the whole trail length L. It should use the length inside one window, at most about 430 px of straight tube. On that basis the filaments stay under about 40% even at a 40-CSS-px cell. The k[6] length cap never needs to engage, and framework change 3 (backing scale on Vfx) is unnecessary.

The same window correction shows where the real exceedance is: the TUBE PLUS SHEATH, which the spec treats only through the count clause. Per window at 0.053 threshold: 17-CSS-px cell about 11k CSS px^2 (51%); 24 CSS px about 72%; above roughly 30 CSS px it exceeds 21,824. The figures are the tube's thickness plus the sheath above threshold (about 0.27 cell each side at k=0), times about 426. Above ~30 CSS px, compliance rests entirely on 'one flash per ignition, ≤3 ignitions/s'. Two conditions make that true: REIGNITE 334 ms > 1000/3 holds; the claim below does not.

False claim: 'a retarget within REIGNITE keeps the same ignition and age, so no new flash'. A retarget moves the quad. Pixels it uncovers lose the tube and pixels it covers gain it, so a long move and back (e.g. `%` held, or repeated half-page jumps) gives regions near the endpoints an extra opposing pair inside one ignition. This is shared with fire's shipped argument and does not block this spec, but the sentence should not stand.

The flash thresholds in check.py/area.py are not worst case. They assume white-on-black (0.35 encoded) and dark-on-pure-white (0.094). Computed over grounds (sRGB, 10% ΔL with darker < 0.80): a light cursor over a mid-grey ground (encoded ~0.5, reachable under glass with dim_dark 0.22 over any wallpaper) flashes from alpha ≈ 0.186. A black cursor over a ground ~0.95 encoded flashes from ≈ 0.052. baud's own light theme, 0x27 on 0xEF, flashes from ≈ 0.063. The k[6] formula hard-codes t = 0.094. With t = 0.052, gain → 0.094 as q → 0 still flashes, so the formula's bound goes unbounded in L (moot once point 3 is fixed, but the stated '≤ 80% at every font size' is not true as derived).

AXIS FALLBACK POPS, and it is the common case, not an edge case. After the chase ends the driver sets `corners = rect.corners()` (baud-app/src/trail.rs frame(), ~line 190), so C == H exactly for the whole remaining life. The axis then always falls back to `ignition.dir`. After a retarget within REIGNITE that direction is the first move's, so the landed nubs and the last filament stubs rotate to a stale direction at the frame |H-C| crosses 0.25 cell. During a retarget's 10 ms dwell the hole is already at the new cursor while the corners are not, which also swings the axis. Suggest carrying the current Segment's direction (segment start centre → target centre) on Vfx: still pure, and it turns only when the quad itself turns.

Precision is feasible, with scoping. Measured on this Mac's GPU (review-plasma/exp.swift, long.swift, compiled with the default fast-math options): fast sinpi max abs error 1.04e-7 on [-1,1), identical to precise::sinpi, far inside the spec's assumed 2^-13. A full-kernel plasma against an f32 CPU port (sinf/expf, floor-based fract) gives 0-4 one-step-off pixels on 25-cell hops at unit 17/34/68, max error 0.0045 steps. A 55×19-cell diagonal gives 4-8. But a 150-cell move at 34 px gives 35-89 one-step-off pixels (max 0.042 steps): the large phase arguments lose precision and are presumably FMA-contracted. The oracle's allowance is 20 per scene (cells.rs:610), so it holds only for scenes of the oracle's current length. Scope the claim, or scale the allowance with the lit count. This is one GPU; other Apple GPUs' fast sinpi is unmeasured.

Factual error: the effect framework (effect.rs with Effect/Ignition/Vfx, EffectU, Kind::Band/Particle) is COMMITTED at HEAD f202aea ('the fire is one effect of a family'). It is not uncommitted: git status is clean. The framework changes listed are still needed. `Effect::params` is `const fn params(self)`, Ignition carries only `unit`, and there is no fx_particle.

Spec text contradicts its own table: 'their small harmonics drift the other way' holds for filaments 0 and 1 (F2 = -0.85, -1.05). Filament 2 has F2 = +1.20, which flows with its fundamental, toward the head.

Hash correlation: phase ph_0 = fx_unit(fx_hash(seed + 0)). Ion 0's h0 = Hash(seed ^ 0·golden).next() = hash(seed), so filament 0's phase equals ion 0's `along`. Salt one of the two, e.g. seed ^ a constant for the phases.

At 1x (17 px cell) two things fail. Ions: radius 0.04-0.075 × 17 × (0.55-1.0) gives 2-3 px records. At pixel centres the fire_ember disc gives about 12% of glow, so the ions are effectively invisible. Records also snap to whole pixels (effect.rs floors x, y), so small ions judder along their spirals. Vertical moves: half = 0.25 cell, so amp = 2.6 px with 1.1-px-floor cores, and the three filaments merge into one blurred stripe.
fixes: Gate the filaments on the side behind the head, e.g. multiply `fil` by smoothstep(-0.05, 0.05, s) (or by smoothstep(0.0, 0.3, s), which also shortens the converged rod), so nothing is drawn ahead of the cursor. Add an oracle and unit assertion that no band pixel with s < 0 outside the hole exceeds the sheath's value.

A choice on non-block cursors. Either (a) take the braid geometry from the cell AND re-derive the filament gate and taper from the braid envelope (gate |w| ≤ amp + 3·width rather than d0 < 0.15), checking REACH still covers it; or (b) clamp k[0] to the quad's own half-thickness across the axis, accepting that the braid collapses to one line for bar and underline. State which in the spec, and add a scene per cursor shape.

Redo area.py per 341×256 window: in-window length ≤ ~430 px (plus meander), worst-case grounds (thresholds 0.186 light-on-grey, 0.052 dark-on-0.95, 0.063 for baud's light theme). Then delete the k[6] length cap and framework change 3, and make k[6] a constant (0.95). Keep the count-clause argument for the tube at large cells, and state the cell height (~30 CSS px) above which the tube relies on it.
Strike 'a retarget ... so no new flash'. Say instead that a retarget can relight pixels the quad re-covers, shared with fire, and bounded by the area clause at ordinary cell sizes.

Replace the H−C axis and ignition.dir fallback with a direction carried on Vfx from the driver's current Segment (start centre → target centre). The driver has it at take()/retarget, it stays pure, and it cannot pop on landing. Keep a unit test that the axis equals the latest segment's direction after a retarget and after the corners land.
Rewrite open question 1 as a statement: WCAG 2.3.1 passes on area OR count, and the braid passes on area. Drop the 'per-pixel-compliant variant'.

Salt the braid phases (e.g. fx_hash(seed ^ 0xA511E9B3 + i)) so they do not equal ion 0's draw. Fix the F2 prose: filament 2's harmonic flows with the fundamental, or set PX_F2[2] negative if counter-flow is intended.

Ions: raise the radius floor, e.g. unit × max(0.06, ...) or ≥ 2.5 px, or place the disc centre at the true sub-pixel position (pass the fractional offset through uv). Otherwise 1x ions are invisible and 2x ions judder. Or drop the ions at 1x, which fits open question 5.

In the precision section, replace the 2^-13 margin analysis with the measurement: fast sinpi ≈ 1e-7 on this GPU, 0-8 off pixels on 25-cell and diagonal scenes, 35-89 on a 150-cell scene. Keep the oracle scenes at about 18-25 cells, or scale its 20-pixel allowance with the lit count. Keep precise::sinpi as the fallback if another GPU disagrees.
Correct the framing: the effect framework is committed at f202aea. The risks list should describe changes to HEAD, not to an uncommitted working tree.
licence_issues: None blocking. The re-fetched pinned files match the spec's sha256: orbkit shdr-13 43c81379…, shdr-14 e81e7bcb…, CREDITS 997c5b96…, LICENSE-SHADERS 3144b714…, Second Reality UNLICENSE 7e12e5df…. CREDITS.md at 5dbd641e lists shdr-13 and shdr-14 among the 14 MIT originals, and the XorDev non-commercial set does not include them. The MIT status of shdr-13 is asserted only by the repository itself, created 2026-09-04, whose other 19 orbs are non-commercial XorDev ports. baud takes the idea only (a zero-set filament, rooted by a smoothstep) and no code, so this is informational.

Nothing from GPL kitty (cursor-trail-lightning.slang, blaze) was lifted. The spec's perpendicular-displacement braid shares only the generic idea of displacing a line perpendicular to the path. kitty uses piecewise-linear hashed nodes, a sin(pi t) envelope and flicker sin(age·95); the plasma uses smooth sums of sines with Gaussian cores. The PX_* constants are original.

fielding/electric.glsl (no licence) and the nimitz Plasma Globe via Shadertweak (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 content) are correctly marked ideas-only, and no code or constants from them appear in the sketch. Lode's page (all rights reserved) contributed prose only.
